title: Which special move applies
origin: foundation worker (combiner node added after a lesson and items asked for a mixed special-move check)

D0.outcome: Names the three special moves (castling, en passant, promotion) and what makes each one possible.

D1.outcome: Told which special move to look for, finds it in a position.

D2.outcome: In mixed positions where nobody names the move, says which special move (if any) is available to the side to move.

misconceptions: A special move is always available when the pieces are in place.
Only one kind of special move can ever be on the board.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S1 (FND.SPECIAL split into castle/en passant/promote; this node is the mixed 'which one?' check added by the foundation worker)
conditions: Each special move has its own condition: castling needs unmoved king and rook with a clear, unattacked path; en passant needs a two-square advance on the previous move; promotion needs a pawn on the last rank.
A position can offer none of them, and the correct answer is then 'none'.
contrasts: A position that looks like en passant but the double-step happened two moves ago.
The rest of the pieces, for deciding which special move is legal.
